title: Enhancing Motivation in Neurorehabilitation: The Impact of Increased Walking Activity on the Reward System and Motor Learning after Stroke
summary:
After a stroke, many people find it difficult to stay motivated and actively participate in rehabilitation. This study investigates whether a targeted increase in daily physical activity, specifically doubling the daily step count, can improve motivation and motor learning.
During the study, participants wear a fitness tracker that records not only step count but also heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV), which reflects fluctuations between heartbeats. These fluctuations provide information about how well the body adapts to physical exertion.
All participants complete two phases: one week with their usual level of activity and one week with increased activity. Throughout the study, reaction time, learning ability, mood and brain activity are assessed.
The aim is to determine whether increased physical activity activates the brain’s reward system and motor-related areas, thereby supporting rehabilitation after a stroke.
conditions: Sequelae of stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction

interventions.name: The study is conducted as a randomized cross-over trial with post-stroke patients 3-6mth after stroke, ensuring that all participants complete both a phase of increased physical activity and a phase of usual daily activity. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minor ischemic stroke within the past 80–190 days
NIHSS < 6 at the time of examination
mRS < 3 (mild to moderate impairment)
Exclusion criteria:
history of neurological disorders
memory problems
psychotropic medication
signs of dementia (MoCA < 23 points)
alcohol abuse, other substance dependencies
inability to provide informed consent
